description: This course introduces students to the theory and application of optimization methods used in engineering, robotics, and intelligent systems. It covers classical optimization, linear and nonlinear programming, numerical techniques, and advanced metaheuristic algorithms. Students also explore soft computing tools such as fuzzy logic and neural networks for intelligent decision-making, with emphasis on mathematical formulation, algorithmic implementation, and solving real-world engineering optimization problems.

syllabus.title: Fundamentals of Optimization
syllabus.body: Introduction: Optimization in engineering and robotics, Problem formulation: Decision variables, objective functions, constraints, Classification: Linear, nonlinear, integer, combinatorial, multi-objective, Classical optimization: Unconstrained and constrained methods.

syllabus.title: Linear and Nonlinear Programming
syllabus.body: Linear Programming: Graphical, Simplex, Big-M, Two-phase, Sensitivity analysis, Nonlinear Programming: Gradient-based, Penalty and barrier methods, Integer & Mixed-Integer Programming.

syllabus.title: Numerical Optimization and Specialized Methods
syllabus.body: Golden Section and Fibonacci search, Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP), Interior Point Methods, Multi-objective optimization.

syllabus.title: Metaheuristic Optimization Techniques
syllabus.body: Genetic Algorithms (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Simulated Annealing (SA), Overview of ACO, ABC, Firefly, GWO, DE.

syllabus.title: Soft Computing Techniques
syllabus.body: Fuzzy Logic: Sets, membership functions, rules, inference, defuzzification. ANN: Neuron model, MLP, Backpropagation, Applications.

outcomes: Apply linear and nonlinear programming techniques.
Apply fuzzy logic and neural networks.
